about: Everything FORCE has met, concepts and sources, and how far we went with each one. Edit this file, then run `npm run topics`. The format is described in .claude/skills/topic/SKILL.md.

mentioned.title: Mentioned
mentioned.description: Only the name so far: still to explore

seen.title: Seen
seen.description: We can say what it is and why it exists, in two sentences

studied.title: Studied
studied.description: We can explain how it works, with an example, and when it fails: it has a page of ours

physics.title: Physics
physics.description: How things move, collide and stay together

math.title: Math
math.description: The math behind motion: change over time, rotations, numbers on a computer

gpu.title: GPU
gpu.description: WebGPU, WGSL and how to make thousands of threads work

engine.title: Engine design
engine.description: How an engine is organized, measured and scaled across devices

method.title: Method
method.description: How we learn and write things down

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: Claude opened it to check what we cite: other topics in it may be missing from the map

full.title: In full
full.description: Claude read all of it, and put on the map every topic in it that matters for FORCE

topics.title: Physics engine
topics.summary: A program that works out how objects move, one small step at a time

topics.title: Simulation step
topics.summary: What an engine repeats over and over: apply forces, find contacts, fix them, move everything

topics.title: Timestep
topics.summary: The jump in time of each step, often 1/60 of a second

topics.title: Fixed timestep
topics.summary: Keeping every step the same length, and spending the time of each frame in equal steps

topics.title: Forces
topics.summary: Pushes such as gravity or wind: they change velocity, and change a light object more than a heavy one

topics.title: Gravity
topics.summary: The force that pulls everything down: on Earth it adds 9.81 m/s of downward speed every second

topics.title: Collision detection
topics.summary: Finding out which objects touch: first a rough pass, then a precise one

topics.title: Broad phase
topics.summary: A rough check that discards pairs of objects too far apart to touch

topics.title: Bounding box
topics.summary: An invisible box around an object: testing two boxes is much cheaper than testing two real shapes

topics.title: Narrow phase
topics.summary: A precise check, on the real shapes, of the pairs that survived the broad phase

topics.title: Tunneling
topics.summary: A fast object passing through a wall between two steps, without ever touching it

topics.title: Contact
topics.summary: The result of a collision: where two objects touch, in which direction, and how far they overlap

topics.title: Constraint
topics.summary: A rule objects must obey, such as "do not pass through each other"

topics.title: Solver
topics.summary: The part of the engine that corrects velocities so constraints are obeyed

topics.title: Iterative solver
topics.summary: Fixing one constraint at a time, going over all of them a few rounds, and stopping when it looks right

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Moving a simulation forward in small steps, updating velocity and position from the current state

topics.title: Particle
topics.summary: A point that moves but has no size or shape: the simplest thing to simulate

topics.title: Rigid body
topics.summary: An object that moves and rotates but never bends, like a box or a ball

topics.title: Spring
topics.summary: A link that keeps two points near a rest distance, pulling when stretched and pushing when squeezed

topics.title: Cloth
topics.summary: A sheet that bends and folds, like a flag or a curtain

topics.title: Fluid
topics.summary: Water, smoke and anything else that flows instead of keeping its shape

topics.title: Parallel work on the GPU
topics.summary: The GPU runs the same code on thousands of items at once, and is fastest when each one can go its own way

topics.title: WebGPU
topics.summary: The browser API that lets a page use the GPU, both to draw and to calculate

topics.title: Adapter and device
topics.summary: How a page gets the GPU: the adapter stands for a GPU on the system, the device is our own connection to it

topics.title: Compute shader
topics.summary: A GPU program that calculates instead of drawing: one function run by many threads at once, each with its own number, reading and writing buffers

topics.title: WGSL
topics.summary: The shader language of WebGPU, the counterpart of GLSL

topics.title: Buffer
topics.summary: A block of GPU memory holding raw bytes, declared up front with everything it will be used for

topics.title: Compute pipeline
topics.summary: A shader made ready to run: one module, one entry point, values for its constants and a layout for its buffers, compiled once and never changed

topics.title: Bind group
topics.summary: Connects real buffers to the numbered slots a shader reads from

topics.title: Workgroups and dispatch
topics.summary: How the work is split into groups of threads and launched on the GPU

topics.title: Commands and queue
topics.summary: GPU work is recorded first, and runs only when it is submitted to the queue

topics.title: Readback
topics.summary: Copying results from the GPU back into JavaScript

topics.title: Position based dynamics (PBD)
topics.summary: Moving points straight to where the constraints want them, instead of going through forces: simple and stable

topics.title: Soft body
topics.summary: An object that squashes and bounces back, like jelly

topics.title: Sweep and prune
topics.summary: A broad phase that sorts objects along an axis, so only neighbours in the list need checking

topics.title: Bounding volume hierarchy (BVH)
topics.summary: Boxes nested inside boxes: a tree that skips whole groups of far-away objects at once

topics.title: Joint
topics.summary: A link that holds two bodies together but lets them move in some ways, like a hinge

topics.title: Implicit integration
topics.summary: Uses the force at the end of the step: stable with stiff springs, but it must solve equations and it drains energy

topics.title: Grid fluid (Eulerian)
topics.summary: A fluid simulated on a fixed grid, tracking what flows through each cell

topics.title: FLIP water
topics.summary: Water simulated with particles that carry the motion, plus a grid that keeps it from compressing

topics.title: Kinds of documentation
topics.summary: Texts for learning, for doing, for looking up and for understanding work best kept apart

topics.title: Derivative
topics.summary: How fast a quantity changes at an instant: velocity is the derivative of position, acceleration that of velocity

topics.title: Integral
topics.summary: The reverse of a derivative: adding up small changes over time, such as velocity into position

topics.title: Floating point precision
topics.summary: Numbers on a computer have a limited number of digits: 32-bit floats are fast on the GPU, but rounding errors add up

topics.title: Explicit Euler
topics.summary: Move with the old velocity, then update the velocity: simple, but it makes oscillations gain energy

topics.title: Semi-implicit Euler
topics.summary: Update the velocity first, then move with the new one: a small swap that keeps a spring's energy bounded when the step is small enough

topics.title: Velocity Verlet
topics.summary: Uses the acceleration both before and after moving: more accurate, but forces are computed twice

topics.title: Numerical stability
topics.summary: Whether a simulation's errors stay small or grow until it explodes: not the same thing as accuracy

topics.title: Stiffness
topics.summary: How strongly a spring or constraint resists: the stiffer it is, the faster it oscillates and the smaller the safe timestep

topics.title: Substepping
topics.summary: Splitting each step into smaller ones, to follow fast motion and stiff constraints

topics.title: Time accumulator
topics.summary: Keeps the real time not simulated yet, and spends it in fixed steps

topics.title: Render interpolation
topics.summary: Drawing a blend of the last two physics states, so motion looks smooth between steps

topics.title: Spiral of death
topics.summary: When catching up on physics takes so long that every frame falls further behind

topics.title: Newton's second law
topics.summary: Force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma): the same push moves a light object more

topics.title: Hooke's law
topics.summary: A spring pulls back in proportion to how far it is stretched (F = −kx)

topics.title: Conservation of energy
topics.summary: Without friction, the energy of motion plus the stored energy stays constant: a simple test for an integrator

topics.title: Plausibility over accuracy
topics.summary: Games need motion that looks right, fast and stable, more than exact physics

topics.title: Center of mass
topics.summary: The balance point of an object: a rigid body's position, and the point it spins around when free

topics.title: Torque
topics.summary: The turning effect of a force: the same push turns more the farther it is from the center (τ = r × F)

topics.title: Moment of inertia
topics.summary: How hard an object is to spin: it depends on its mass and on how far that mass is from the axis

topics.title: Inertia tensor
topics.summary: The moment of inertia in 3D: a 3×3 matrix, because the resistance to spinning changes with the axis

topics.title: Angular velocity
topics.summary: How fast a body spins and around which axis, as one vector in radians per second

topics.title: Angular momentum
topics.summary: Inertia times angular velocity: the quantity a torque changes over time

topics.title: Orientation
topics.summary: How a body is rotated, stored as a quaternion and updated each step by a small rotation

topics.title: Inverse mass
topics.summary: Storing 1/m instead of m: no divisions in hot loops, and zero means a body that never moves

topics.title: Uniform grid
topics.summary: Space split into equal cells: only objects in the same or nearby cells get compared

topics.title: Spatial hashing
topics.summary: A uniform grid stored in a hash table, so it can cover endless space with little memory

topics.title: GJK
topics.summary: A test that tells whether two convex shapes overlap, using only their farthest points in each direction

topics.title: EPA
topics.summary: Run after GJK when two shapes overlap, to find how deep and in which direction

topics.title: Signed distance field collision
topics.summary: Describing a shape by the distance from it at every point of space, so a contact test becomes a lookup

topics.title: Continuous collision detection
topics.summary: Checking the whole path between two steps, so fast objects cannot tunnel through walls

topics.title: Contact manifold
topics.summary: All the contact points between two touching shapes, such as the four corners of a box resting on the floor

topics.title: Friction
topics.summary: The force that resists sliding between two surfaces in contact

topics.title: Restitution
topics.summary: How bouncy a collision is: how much speed comes back after the impact

topics.title: Raycast
topics.summary: Shooting a line into the world to find what it hits first, for aiming, picking or line of sight

topics.title: Contact events
topics.summary: Telling game code when two objects start or stop touching

topics.title: Impulse-based dynamics
topics.summary: Resolving collisions by changing velocities at once, with an instant kick called an impulse

topics.title: Sequential impulses (PGS)
topics.summary: Applying impulses to one contact or joint at a time, over several rounds: the classic rigid body solver

topics.title: Gauss-Seidel
topics.summary: Fixing constraints one after another, each using the latest results: converges fast, but it is sequential

topics.title: Jacobi
topics.summary: Fixing every constraint at once from the same old state, then combining: parallel, but slower to converge

topics.title: TGS solver
topics.summary: PhysX's temporal Gauss-Seidel solver, designed to converge better with complex constraints

topics.title: Warm starting
topics.summary: Starting the solver from the previous step's answer, so fewer rounds are needed

topics.title: Islands
topics.summary: Groups of bodies that touch each other, solved apart from the rest

topics.title: Sleeping
topics.summary: Pausing bodies that have come to rest, until something wakes them up

topics.title: Soft Step
topics.summary: The solver of recent Box2D versions, built around substeps

topics.title: Distance constraint
topics.summary: A rule that keeps two points at a fixed distance: the building block of chains, ropes and cloth

topics.title: Constraint graph coloring
topics.summary: Splitting constraints into groups that share no body, so each group can be solved in parallel

topics.title: XPBD
topics.summary: Extended PBD: each constraint gets a softness, called compliance, so stiffness no longer depends on step size or rounds

topics.title: Shape matching
topics.summary: Pulling a group of particles back toward the best rigid fit of their original shape

topics.title: Unified particle physics
topics.summary: Building every material, from solids to cloth and fluids, out of particles held by constraints

topics.title: Mesh sampling
topics.summary: Turning a mesh's surface or volume into points, for example to build a body out of particles

topics.title: Mass-spring system
topics.summary: Particles linked by springs: the simplest model of cloth and soft bodies

topics.title: Finite element method (FEM)
topics.summary: Splitting a solid into small pieces, such as tetrahedra, and working out how each one deforms

topics.title: Self-collision
topics.summary: Cloth or a soft body hitting itself

topics.title: SPH
topics.summary: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics: a fluid's density and pressure at each particle, estimated from its neighbours

topics.title: Position based fluids (PBF)
topics.summary: Fluids kept from compressing with position constraints, the PBD way

topics.title: Material point method (MPM)
topics.summary: Particles carry the material while a grid works out the forces: good for snow, sand and deformables

topics.title: Neighbour search
topics.summary: Finding the particles near each particle: a major cost of particle fluids

topics.title: Granular materials
topics.summary: Sand, snow and grains: solid up close, flowing in bulk

topics.title: Two-way coupling
topics.summary: Different materials pushing on each other both ways, like a ball floating on water

topics.title: Destruction
topics.summary: Breaking objects into pieces while the game runs

topics.title: Articulated bodies
topics.summary: Chains of bodies linked by joints, such as robots and ragdolls

topics.title: Atomic operations
topics.summary: Memory updates that stay correct even when thousands of threads write to the same place

topics.title: Determinism
topics.summary: Two runs from the same start give exactly the same numbers. On the GPU, threads adding floats to the same body in a different order each run can break it

topics.title: Prefix sum (scan)
topics.summary: Turning a list of counts into running totals, in parallel: the GPU's way of packing results

topics.title: Parallel sorting
topics.summary: Sorting many keys at once on the GPU, for example objects by grid cell

topics.title: Structure of arrays (SoA)
topics.summary: One array per property, all positions together and all velocities together, instead of one object per particle

topics.title: GPU-resident simulation
topics.summary: Keeping the simulation's data on the GPU, and not reading it back every frame

topics.title: Device limits
topics.summary: What a given GPU guarantees, such as buffer sizes and workgroup memory: to check before choosing a pipeline

topics.title: Compatibility mode
topics.summary: A restricted WebGPU that also runs on older graphics APIs, such as OpenGL ES 3.1

topics.title: Quality tiers
topics.summary: The same simulation at different costs: fewer particles, substeps and solver rounds on weaker devices

topics.title: Frame budget
topics.summary: The slice of each frame the physics may use, for example 2 to 4 ms of the 16.7 ms available at 60 FPS

topics.title: Benchmark scenes
topics.summary: Standard test scenes, such as a stack of boxes or a dam break, to compare algorithms fairly

topics.title: Thermal throttling
topics.summary: Phones slow down as they heat up, so speed must be measured over minutes, not seconds

topics.title: Entity component system (ECS)
topics.summary: Organizing a game as plain data components processed by systems, instead of objects with methods

topics.title: Job system
topics.summary: Splitting the work of a step into small jobs spread over the CPU cores

topics.title: Symplectic integrator
topics.summary: An integrator that keeps energy steady on average over long runs, such as semi-implicit Euler or Verlet

topics.title: Runge-Kutta 4 (RK4)
topics.summary: Samples the rate of change four times per step: very accurate, but four times the work, and it slowly loses energy

topics.title: Semi-fixed timestep
topics.summary: Splitting long frames into steps no longer than a maximum: safer, but steps still differ in length

topics.title: Particle-based rigid bodies
topics.summary: A rigid body's shape approximated by spheres, so every collision becomes a cheap test between spheres

topics.title: Discrete element method (DEM)
topics.summary: Particles that push each other apart when they overlap, like small springs, with dampers to absorb the bounce

topics.title: Decision record
topics.summary: A short page per design choice: what we chose, why, and what we left out, so nobody has to accept or reverse it blindly

topics.summary: WGSL code handed to the device and compiled; a mistake in it does not throw, and getCompilationInfo() gives the compiler's messages

topics.title: WGSL specification, §7.2 Value Declarations
topics.summary: The names that stand for a value and never change (const, override, let, function parameters), and the moment each one is fixed

topics.title: WGSL specification, §7.3 var Declarations
topics.summary: Variables as named memory: where the memory lives (address space), who may write it (access mode), how long it lasts and what it holds at the start

topics.title: Value declaration
topics.summary: A name for a value that can never change and has no memory behind it: const, override, let and function parameters

topics.title: Shader lifecycle
topics.summary: The four moments in the life of a shader: its code becomes a module, the module becomes a pipeline, a draw or dispatch starts it, and it ends when every thread is done. Each kind of constant is fixed at one of them

topics.title: const declaration
topics.summary: A WGSL constant fixed when the shader is compiled: it needs a value the compiler can work out by itself

topics.title: Const-expression
topics.summary: An expression the compiler can evaluate while compiling the shader, such as 2 * 3 or vec3(1, 2, 3)

topics.title: Abstract numeric types
topics.summary: The types of numbers written without a suffix (AbstractInt, AbstractFloat): they adapt to i32, u32 or f32 where they are used, which the spec calls concretization

topics.title: Constructible type
topics.summary: A type whose values can be created, copied and passed around: scalars, vectors, matrices, fixed-size arrays and structs made of them

topics.title: Override-expression
topics.summary: An expression built from override constants, known only when the pipeline is created: it can size an array or a workgroup

topics.title: Pipeline constant ID
topics.summary: The @id(n) attribute gives an override a number, and JavaScript then sets it by that number and not by its name

topics.title: let declaration
topics.summary: A name for a value computed while the shader runs and fixed from then on: only inside functions, and it can also hold a pointer

topics.title: Module and function scope
topics.summary: Where a name can be used: everywhere in the shader if declared outside functions, or from its line to the closing brace if declared inside one

topics.title: References and pointers
topics.summary: A variable is a reference to memory, typed ref<address space, type, access mode>: reading it is a load, assigning to it a store, and & turns it into a pointer. Values have no memory, so no pointer

topics.title: var declaration
topics.summary: The only thing that can change in WGSL: a name for a piece of memory holding a value of one type (the store type)

topics.title: Address space
topics.summary: Where a variable's memory lives, written var<…>: function, private, workgroup, uniform, storage, immediate, or handle for textures and samplers

topics.title: Access mode
topics.summary: Whether a variable's memory can be read, written or both. Only storage buffers let you choose, and they are read-only unless you write read_write

topics.title: Storage buffer
topics.summary: A buffer seen from the shader as var<storage>: it can be big, hold an array with no fixed length, and be written by the threads

topics.title: Workgroup variable
topics.summary: A var<workgroup>: memory shared by the threads of one workgroup, only in compute shaders, starting at zero

topics.title: Private variable
topics.summary: A var<private>: a global variable of which every thread gets its own separate copy

topics.title: Immediate data
topics.summary: A var<immediate>: a few values set straight from the command encoder with setImmediates, with no buffer to create

topics.title: Textures and samplers in WGSL
topics.summary: Module-scope variables holding an opaque handle to a texture or a sampler; a storage texture can also be written, with textureStore

topics.title: Resource interface
topics.summary: Everything a shader expects from outside: its uniform buffers, storage buffers, textures and samplers, each with a @group and a @binding

topics.title: Host-shareable type
topics.summary: A type with a fixed layout in bytes, so JavaScript and the shader agree on it: the only kind allowed in a buffer

topics.title: Variable lifetime
topics.summary: How long a variable keeps its memory: the whole run of the shader for globals, its block for locals. Two live variables never share memory, apart from resources

topics.title: Zero value
topics.summary: What a variable holds when it is declared with no initial value: all zeros, never garbage

topics.title: WGSL specification, §2.1 Shader Lifecycle
topics.summary: The four moments in the life of a shader: module creation, pipeline creation, execution start, execution end

topics.title: Entry point
topics.summary: The function where a shader starts, marked @compute, @vertex or @fragment. A pipeline compiles only the code its entry point reaches: the rest of the module is dropped

topics.title: Shader stage
topics.summary: The kind of work a shader does in a pipeline: vertex, fragment or compute. Each stage is compiled on its own, even from the same module

topics.title: Render pipeline
topics.summary: The pipeline that draws: a vertex and a fragment shader plus their fixed settings, made with createRenderPipeline()

topics.title: Invocation
topics.summary: One run of an entry point: what our guides call a thread. A dispatch or a draw starts many, and the shader ends when all are done

topics.title: Pipeline layout
topics.summary: Which buffers a pipeline expects and in which slots. 'auto' works it out from the shader, but its bind groups then work with that pipeline only; one made by hand with createPipelineLayout() can be given to several pipelines, which then share bind groups

topics.title: Async pipeline creation
topics.summary: createComputePipelineAsync() returns a promise that resolves when the pipeline is compiled. It is not faster: it lets the rest of the GPU work go on meanwhile, and a mistake rejects the promise with a GPUPipelineError

topics.title: WebGPU specification, §10 Pipelines
topics.summary: What a pipeline is, the immediate and the async way to create one, how constants get their values, and what the 'auto' layout holds

topics.title: MDN, GPUDevice.createComputePipeline()
topics.summary: The descriptor of a compute pipeline, and what makes it invalid

topics.title: MDN, GPUDevice.createComputePipelineAsync()
topics.summary: The promise version, and the GPUPipelineError it rejects with

topics.title: three.js r187, WebGLRenderer.js
topics.summary: compile() and compileAsync() build a scene's shader programs before the first frame: the three.js parallel of creating a pipeline ahead of time

topics.title: three.js r187, WebGLPrograms.js
topics.summary: A material's defines are part of the key that tells one compiled program from another

topics.title: Timelines
topics.summary: The three places where WebGPU work happens: your script (content), the browser's part that creates GPU objects, often another process (device), and the GPU itself (queue). Why most calls return before the work is done

topics.title: Shader cache
topics.summary: Browsers keep what they have compiled: in Chrome a shader text seen before took 0.3 ms instead of 141. It makes naive timings lie

topics.title: WebGPU specification, §3.4.1 Timelines
topics.summary: Content, device and queue timeline: which work happens where, and why async calls exist

topics.title: Firefox bug 1878449, comment 5
topics.summary: A Firefox engineer gives the async pipeline methods as best practice: the immediate ones are hard to keep from blocking the work that follows

topics.title: Bind group layout
topics.summary: The description of the slots of one bind group: for each binding, what kind of resource goes there and which shader stages see it. Made by hand with createBindGroupLayout(), or taken from a pipeline

topics.title: Force-directed layout
topics.summary: Placing the nodes of a graph with a simulation: links pull like springs, and every node pushes the others away

topics.title: d3-force-3d
topics.summary: A small library that simulates forces between points in 1, 2 or 3 dimensions, made to lay out graphs
